passage.text: Every city has its ghost stories, and Bangkok is no different.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈsɪti ˈhæz ɪts ˈɡoʊst ˌstɔːriz, ənd ˈbæŋkɑːk ɪz ˈnoʊ ˈdɪfərənt.

passage.text: One of the most famous is the story of the old Golden Star movie theater near Chinatown.
passage.reading: ˈwʌn əv ðə ˈmoʊst ˈfeɪməs ɪz ðə ˈstɔːri əv ði ˈoʊld ˈɡoʊldən ˈstɑːr ˈmuːvi ˌθiːətər ˈnɪr ˈtʃaɪnətaʊn.

passage.text: It opened in 1960 and closed thirty years later.
passage.reading: ɪt ˈoʊpənd ɪn ˈnaɪntiːn ˈsɪksti ənd ˈkloʊzd ˈθɜːrti ˈjɪrz ˈleɪtər.

passage.text: According to the legend, a young woman sold tickets there in the 1970s.
passage.reading: əˈkɔːrdɪŋ tə ðə ˈlɛdʒənd, ə ˈjʌŋ ˈwʊmən ˈsoʊld ˈtɪkɪts ˈðɛr ɪn ðə ˈnaɪntiːn ˈsɛvəntiz.

passage.text: Every night, she would wait for the man she loved after the last movie.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈnaɪt, ʃiː wʊd ˈweɪt fər ðə ˈmæn ʃiː ˈlʌvd ˈæftər ðə ˈlæst ˈmuːvi.

passage.text: But one night, he never came, and she was never seen again.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈwʌn ˈnaɪt, hiː ˈnɛvər ˈkeɪm, ənd ʃiː wʌz ˈnɛvər ˈsiːn əˈɡɛn.

passage.text: After the theater closed, people started to hear strange things.
passage.reading: ˈæftər ðə ˈθiːətər ˈkloʊzd, ˈpiːpəl ˈstɑːrtɪd tə ˈhɪr ˈstreɪndʒ ˈθɪŋz.

passage.text: Night guards said that they heard a woman whispering in the empty building: "Is he here yet?"
passage.reading: ˈnaɪt ˈɡɑːrdz ˈsɛd ðæt ðeɪ ˈhɜːrd ə ˈwʊmən ˈwɪspərɪŋ ɪn ði ˈɛmpti ˈbɪldɪŋ: ɪz hiː ˈhɪr ˈjɛt?

passage.text: Others claimed that they had seen a woman in an old uniform near the ticket office.
passage.reading: ˈʌðərz ˈkleɪmd ðæt ðeɪ hæd ˈsiːn ə ˈwʊmən ɪn ən ˈoʊld ˈjuːnəfɔːrm ˈnɪr ðə ˈtɪkɪt ˌɔːfɪs.

passage.text: Today, there is a spirit house in front of the old building.
passage.reading: təˈdeɪ, ðɛr ɪz ə ˈspɪrɪt ˌhaʊs ɪn ˈfrʌnt əv ði ˈoʊld ˈbɪldɪŋ.

passage.text: Every morning, people leave offerings there: flowers, red drinks and small cakes.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈmɔːrnɪŋ, ˈpiːpəl ˈliːv ˈɔːfərɪŋz ˈðɛr: ˈflaʊərz, ˈrɛd ˈdrɪŋks ənd ˈsmɔːl ˈkeɪks.

passage.text: Many people don't, but they still bring an offering when they walk past the spirit house, just in case.
passage.reading: ˈmɛni ˈpiːpəl ˈdoʊnt, bʌt ðeɪ ˈstɪl ˈbrɪŋ ən ˈɔːfərɪŋ wɛn ðeɪ ˈwɔːk ˈpæst ðə ˈspɪrɪt ˌhaʊs, ˈdʒʌst ɪn ˈkeɪs.
